title: [Perf] Skip TP all-reduce of sampled token ids when world size is 1
body:
## Motivation

The sampler all-reduces the sampled token ids across the TP group to mask nondeterminism from operators that are not guaranteed to be bit-identical across ranks. With a single rank the reduce is a no-op, but the collective still allocates GPU memory for the communication. On small-memory cards that allocation can push the process past its limit and OOM, so skip it entirely.

Store the TP group (not just its device_group) on the Sampler and bail out of the all-reduce when world_size == 1 or the device group is absent.

### Description
While profiling on NSYS the Triton `_rms_norm_tiled_onepass` kernel on an NVIDIA A10G for large hidden dimensions ( `S=4096, D=4096`), I observed severe register pressure and very low occupancy.

The current heuristic `block_size_seq = min(16, triton.next_power_of_2(max(1, S // 512)))` forces `BLOCK_SIZE_SEQ=8` for `S=4096`.

1. Removed the hardcoded `block_size_seq` heuristic.

The roadmap (#26693) lists an asynchronous/event-driven NIXL backend under
Performance: "The NIXL backend currently polls on the transfer completion. We
think we can do better. State: Early planning. Needs some benchmarks first, not
clear it can be justified." This PR adds that benchmark.

## Purpose

MRV2 stores generated-token counts in a persistent
`[max_num_reqs, vocab_size]` int32 tensor. When `max_model_len <= 65535`, each
count fits exactly in uint16.

This change:

- uses uint16 counts for those configurations and keeps int32 for longer contexts;
- pads odd vocab sizes so two uint16 counters can share one int32 atomic word;
